framework.name: MECE Principle
framework.one_liner: Cuts a whole into branches on one dimension so that nothing overlaps and nothing is left out; the branch that comes back empty is the underserved market.

slots.label: Whole
slots.description: The thing being partitioned: a market, a spend, a problem, a population. Its size is what the branches must add up to.

slots.label: Cut
slots.description: The single dimension the whole is cut on. Choosing it is the whole of MECE: one cut gives exclusive branches, two cuts at once give overlaps.

slots.label: Bucket
slots.description: A branch of the partition. Usually the analyst's construction rather than the source's, even when the source names the members.

slots.label: Item
slots.description: An observed member placed in a bucket: a company, a ledger line, a customer type. This is where the source's own words live.

slots.label: Gap
slots.description: A branch the data leaves empty or thin: no member, or no member that counts. The candidate blind spot, and in a market the candidate underserved space.

slots.label: Overlap
slots.description: An item or a branch that lands in two buckets at once. Always a symptom of two dimensions mixed into one cut.

relations.label: cut by
relations.description: the whole, or a branch of it, is cut by one partitioning dimension

relations.label: partitions into
relations.description: the whole, under the chosen cut, partitions into buckets

relations.label: missing from
relations.description: what the partition does not hold: an unopened branch of the cut, an absent member of a bucket, or a share of the whole that no branch accounts for

relations.label: violates
relations.description: an overlap violates exclusivity between buckets, or the cut that was supposed to keep them apart

examples.title: Where did every case go? A drinks company's volume, cut one way
examples.summary: A ledger of last year's case volume is read out in a meeting. The lines are facts; the channel partition, the double-counted wholesaler and the branch nobody has ever opened are the analysis.

source.title: Minutes of a strategy meeting at a bottled-drinks company
source.text: Minutes of a Monday strategy meeting at a mid-size bottled-drinks company. The finance director reads last year's volume from the ledger: the company shipped 4.1 million cases in total, down from 4.6 million the year before. Supermarket chains took 1.7 million cases and convenience stores took 0.9 million. The company's own website shipped 0.2 million cases direct to consumers, and vending operators took 0.3 million. The sales director adds that a further 0.4 million cases went to a German wholesaler, and that nobody is sure whether those cases ended up in shops or in restaurants, because the wholesaler is booked by country and not by channel. The finance director notes that the ledger's lines do not add up to the total and asks what the remaining cases were; nobody in the room can say. The head of marketing observes that the company has no salesperson who calls on restaurants, canteens or hotels, and that the ledger has never had a line for them. The CEO closes the meeting by asking for one picture of where every case goes, cut one way only, before the board meets.
source.attribution: A written-out version of the standard MECE teaching case: a volume or cost base whose reported lines neither add up nor stay apart. The test is Barbara Minto's.

nodes.label: 4.1m cases shipped last year
nodes.text: The whole to be partitioned is last year's shipped volume: 4.1 million cases in total, down from 4.6 million the year before.
nodes.source_quote: the company shipped 4.1 million cases in total

nodes.label: One picture, cut one way only
nodes.text: The CEO asks for one picture of where every case goes, cut one way only. That is the MECE instruction, and it is all the source gives: the rule, not the dimension.
nodes.source_quote: asking for one picture of where every case goes, cut one way only

nodes.label: Cut by channel
nodes.text: The dimension chosen is channel: where the case is sold, not who bought it, not which country it went to. Every branch below is a channel and nothing else.
nodes.rationale: The CEO demands one cut but never says which. Channel is the dimension four of the five ledger lines already follow (supermarkets, convenience, own website, vending), so it is the cut that costs the least re-coding, and it is the cut that makes the German line's ambiguity visible instead of hiding it inside a geography branch.

nodes.label: Grocery retail
nodes.text: Off-trade grocery: cases sold through shops a household buys from, whether a supermarket chain or a convenience store.
nodes.rationale: The ledger keeps supermarkets and convenience stores as two lines. Merging them into one branch is the analyst's move; it is justified because both sell the same pack to the same drinker through the same route to market, and separating them would cut on account size, which is a second dimension.

nodes.label: Direct to consumer
nodes.text: Cases the company ships itself to the drinker, with no retailer in between.
nodes.rationale: The website line is one ledger row; calling it a branch of the channel cut is the analyst's construction, and it is what makes the 0.2 million comparable with the 1.7 million rather than a footnote.

nodes.label: Vending
nodes.text: Cases sold through vending operators, who place the machines and buy the stock.
nodes.rationale: Vending is a distinct route to market with its own economics; the ledger names the operators but never calls them a channel. As a branch it stays exclusive of grocery because a case cannot be both machine-filled and shelf-stocked.

nodes.label: On-premise: branch never opened
nodes.text: The fourth channel a drinks business always has, restaurants, canteens and hotels, where the drink is consumed where it is bought. Under this cut it is a branch with no ledger line, no salesperson and no number.
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the minutes says the on-premise channel exists. It is the branch the cut requires in order to be collectively exhaustive: once channel is the dimension, off-trade and on-trade are the two halves of it, and the source has only ever counted the off-trade half.

nodes.label: Supermarket chains, 1.7m
nodes.text: Supermarket chains took 1.7 million cases, the largest single line in the ledger.
nodes.source_quote: Supermarket chains took 1.7 million cases

nodes.label: Convenience stores, 0.9m
nodes.text: Convenience stores took 0.9 million cases.
nodes.source_quote: convenience stores took 0.9 million

nodes.label: Own website, 0.2m
nodes.text: The company's own website shipped 0.2 million cases direct to consumers.
nodes.source_quote: The company's own website shipped 0.2 million cases direct to consumers

nodes.label: Vending operators, 0.3m
nodes.text: Vending operators took 0.3 million cases.
nodes.source_quote: vending operators took 0.3 million

nodes.label: German wholesaler, 0.4m
nodes.text: A further 0.4 million cases went to a German wholesaler; nobody is sure whether those cases ended up in shops or in restaurants, because the wholesaler is booked by country and not by channel.
nodes.source_quote: a further 0.4 million cases went to a German wholesaler

nodes.label: No line, no salesperson
nodes.text: The company has no salesperson who calls on restaurants, canteens or hotels, and the ledger has never had a line for them.
nodes.source_quote: the company has no salesperson who calls on restaurants, canteens or hotels, and that the ledger has never had a line for them

nodes.label: 0.6m cases in no branch
nodes.text: The five ledger lines add to 3.5 million cases against a total of 4.1 million: 0.6 million cases, one case in seven, sit in no branch of the partition at all.
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic on the stated numbers: 1.7 + 0.9 + 0.2 + 0.3 + 0.4 = 3.5 against a stated total of 4.1. The minutes say the lines do not add up and that nobody can say what the rest were; the size of the hole, and that it is a seventh of the business, is the inference.

nodes.label: German line cut by country
nodes.text: The German wholesaler line is booked on a different dimension from every other line: country, not channel. Its 0.4 million cases could be in grocery or in on-premise, so as long as it stands the branches are not mutually exclusive.
nodes.rationale: The minutes state the booking basis and the uncertainty but not the diagnosis. Naming it as a second dimension smuggled into a single cut is what turns an accounting annoyance into the reason the partition fails the exclusivity test, and it says what to do: re-code the German cases by channel before the picture is drawn.

edges.source_quote: asking for one picture of where every case goes, cut one way only

edges.rationale: The instruction is stated, the dimension that satisfies it is chosen.
Branch of the channel cut; two ledger lines fold into it.
Branch of the channel cut; one ledger line falls in it.
Branch of the channel cut; one ledger line falls in it.
The branch the cut requires for exhaustiveness and the ledger has never held.
Placing a stated line in a constructed branch is the analyst's act, though this one is near-forced.
Convenience stores are grocery retail on the channel dimension, whatever their account size.
The website line is the direct branch; the source states the line, not the branch.
The operator line is the vending branch; the source states the line, not the branch.
If the German cases went to shops they belong in grocery, and grocery is then understated by up to 0.4 million.
If they went to restaurants they belong in the branch that does not exist, which is why the same 0.4 million can be claimed twice.
The residual is defined against the stated total, so it hangs off the whole and not off any branch.
A stated absence of coverage becomes a hole in the partition only once channel is the dimension; under a geography cut the same sentence would say nothing.
The ledger's own largest line is already a channel, which is why channel is the cheapest cut to impose.
The website line is a channel too, so four of the five lines need no re-coding.
The wholesaler's 0.4 million is inside the 3.5 million that was summed, so the 0.6 million residual is on top of it.
No salesperson and no ledger line is the evidence that the branch was never opened, rather than opened and empty.
The line itself, and the stated fact that it is booked by country, is the whole of the evidence for the defect.
The uncounted channel is the obvious candidate home for the uncounted cases, though the minutes never connect the two.

examples.title: Elad Gil's map of the AI application market: seven named verticals inside a $5 trillion whole
examples.summary: An investor partitions the AI opportunity vertical by vertical and names the finalists in each. The buckets and their members are quoted; the residual branch that holds most of the $5 trillion, and the rule for finding what fills it, are the analysis.

source.episode_title: Sam Altman live on Sora, Hollywood & the future of ads (Bill Peebles, Dylan Patel, Elad Gil, Robby Stein, Morgan Housel, Misha Laskin)

examples.why_this_episode: Elad Gil does the partition out loud. Asked how to think about AI companies, he says the markets have crystallised, runs the AI application market vertical by vertical naming the finalists in each, flags the verticals where the winner is unknown, and separately sizes the whole at about $5 trillion of services. It is a MECE exercise with its two classic defects on the record: a layer (the foundation model companies) is mixed in with the verticals and re-appears inside them, and the branches he can name cover only a sliver of the whole he has stated.

nodes.label: $5T of services AI can enter
nodes.text: The whole being partitioned is the services economy Gil's team sized as the ground AI could intervene in: about $5 trillion, a large share of GDP.
nodes.source_quote: The services economy that we looked at on my team in terms of where AI could intervene is about $5 trillion.

nodes.label: Verticals, not the model layer
nodes.text: The host sets the dimension before the answer starts: the question is about vertical markets, smaller markets, and explicitly not the foundation model layer.
nodes.source_quote: If we're talking vertical markets, smaller markets, not the foundation model layer.

nodes.label: Go vertical by vertical
nodes.text: Gil's own cut: the AI application market is walked one vertical at a time, and each vertical is asked the same question.
nodes.source_quote: And you can go through sort of vertical by vertical.

nodes.label: Second cut: settled or open
nodes.text: A second dimension runs across the first. Each vertical is filed as settled, where it is clear who the finalists are, or open, where the market is clearly important, there are tons of players, and the winners are unknown.
nodes.rationale: Gil applies the same finalists test to every vertical he names but never calls it a dimension. Reading it as a second cut is what turns financial tooling, sales enablement and accounting from a list into a class, and it is the class an investor or a founder is actually choosing between.

nodes.label: Foundation model market
nodes.text: The foundation model market: the first branch Gil files, and the one the host's framing had put outside the question.
nodes.source_quote: We know that for the foundation model market.

nodes.label: Coding
nodes.text: Coding: a settled vertical whose finalists Gil can name without hesitating.
nodes.source_quote: We know for coding, it's cognition, cursor, and then the foundation model companies in Microsoft.

nodes.label: Healthcare
nodes.text: Healthcare: named as one of the verticals now known, with a handful of contenders in it.
nodes.source_quote: There's a bunch of verticals now we know, a bridge for healthcare and maybe commier.

nodes.label: Legal
nodes.text: Legal: solidified, in Gil's reading, except for a handful of narrower sub-verticals such as personal injury.
nodes.source_quote: legal feels like it's already solidified except a handful of these more vertical specific

nodes.label: Financial tooling
nodes.text: Financial tooling: a market Gil is sure will matter, with tons of players in it and no known winner.
nodes.source_quote: And there's tons of players, but we don't know who the winners are. That's financial tooling.

nodes.label: Accounting and sales enablement
nodes.text: Accounting, and sales enablement beside it: the other two branches Gil files under important, crowded and unresolved.
nodes.source_quote: Maybe that's sales enablement. Maybe that's accounting.

nodes.label: Residual: every other service line
nodes.text: The branch nobody opens. Models, coding, healthcare, legal, financial tooling, sales enablement, accounting and customer support are perhaps a few hundred billion dollars of the $5 trillion; the rest of the services economy is one unnamed branch.
nodes.rationale: Gil states a whole of about $5 trillion and names roughly eight verticals, then says you can come up with the list. Nobody closes the partition. Adding the residual branch is what turns a list of markets into a statement about coverage, and every gap below hangs inside it.

nodes.label: Durable systems of record
nodes.text: A branch that is populated and closed: multi-product systems of record whose moat is the cross-sell, not the model, and which an AI-native entrant does not take by being AI-native.
nodes.rationale: Gil says of one company that nobody is going to do the AI-first version and suddenly win. Generalising the one case into a branch of the same partition is the inference, and it matters because it is the part of the $5 trillion that is inside the whole but not inside the opportunity.

nodes.label: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Meta
nodes.text: The finalists Gil names in the foundation model market: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, perhaps xAI, Meta, Mistral and a few others. A small list.
nodes.source_quote: We know it's anthropic, open AI, Google, perhaps XAI, meta, a few others, mistraw, whatever.

nodes.label: Cognition, Cursor, and the labs
nodes.text: The finalists Gil names in coding: Cognition, Cursor, and then the foundation model companies plus Microsoft.
nodes.source_quote: it's cognition, cursor, and then the foundation model companies in Microsoft

nodes.label: Abridge, maybe Commure
nodes.text: The contenders Gil names in healthcare: Abridge, and maybe Commure. Transcribed as a bridge and commier.
nodes.source_quote: a bridge for healthcare and maybe commier

nodes.label: Legal bought no software until AI
nodes.text: Legal never bought any software and was really hard to sell into; because of AI, a legal AI company can suddenly exist. The transcript renders the company as RV.
nodes.source_quote: legal never bought any software. It was really hard to sell into legal, but because of AI, suddenly RV can exist

nodes.label: Support: labor, not seats
nodes.text: Customer support as Gil re-prices it: not how many seats you sell the reps, but how much of their work you do. The labor market versus the software market.
nodes.source_quote: you're looking at, for example, customer support. It's not Zendaz, How many seats can you sell the customer support reps? It's how much can you augment and do work for customer support reps? It's the labor market versus the software market.

nodes.label: Rippling cross-sells a dozen products
nodes.text: Rippling cross-sells a dozen different HR products; AI can make some of them better, but nobody is going to do the AI-first Rippling and suddenly win.
nodes.source_quote: Ripling is an amazing company they uh cross sell a dozen different HR products. And AI can make some stuff better, but nobody's going to do the AI first rippling and suddenly win, right?

nodes.label: The labs are in every bucket
nodes.text: The foundation model companies are a branch of this partition and a member of the coding branch at the same time. Layer and vertical are two dimensions, and mixing them means no vertical branch is exclusive of the model branch.
nodes.rationale: The host explicitly excluded the model layer from the question, and Gil's coding list ends with the foundation model companies. The double count is on the record; naming it as a mixed cut rather than a quirk is the inference, and it carries a rule: every vertical bucket has to be defended against the lab that is already sitting in it.

nodes.label: AI means everything now
nodes.text: Gil states the limit case of the defect himself: AI means everything now, it means consumer, it means roll-ups, it means vertical SaaS. A branch that contains everything is exclusive of nothing.
nodes.source_quote: And AI means everything now. It means consumer. It means roll-ups. It means vertical fast.

nodes.label: Most of the whole has no contender
nodes.text: Add up the verticals anyone in the room can name and you have a small fraction of $5 trillion. The rest of the services economy has no finalist, no crowd and, in this conversation, no name.
nodes.rationale: The arithmetic is forced but the reading is not: coverage is inferred by comparing a stated whole with a list the speaker himself treats as illustrative rather than complete, and the un-named remainder may be un-named because it is unattractive rather than because it is unnoticed.
nodes.idea: The largest AI application segment is the set of service lines nobody at the table can name: where there is neither a finalist nor a crowd, the first credible product defines the category instead of fighting for it, so the highest-yield screen is to list the services economy by payroll and strike out every line that appeared in this conversation.

nodes.label: Verticals that bought no software
nodes.text: The branch with no incumbent is the branch that never bought software in the first place. Legal was one of those until AI made it buyable; the rest of that class is still empty.
nodes.rationale: Gil gives the mechanism for exactly one vertical: legal bought no software, was hard to sell into, and became reachable because of AI. Turning one case into a screen for the whole residual branch is a generalisation, and it is contestable because legal also had unusually high billing rates, which is not true of every software-free trade.
nodes.idea: Screen the services economy for lines with near-zero software spend per worker and high labor spend, such as claims adjusting, freight brokerage, permitting, title work and medical billing appeals, because each one is an empty bucket where an AI-native entrant has no incumbent to displace and no crowd to outspend.

nodes.label: The labor half of every bucket
nodes.text: Every branch here is drawn around a software market and sized by seats. The labor spend for the same work sits in no branch at all, and it is the larger number.
nodes.rationale: Gil states the shift from seat-based value to labor and applies it to customer support. Reading it as a missing branch rather than a pricing note is the inference: if the cut is drawn on software categories, a whole dimension of the $5 trillion has no bucket, which is why the market sizes come out too small.
nodes.idea: Price and size against the labor line rather than the seat line: the open space is any vertical where software spend is near zero and payroll is large, and the product that wins it is sold as work delivered, not as software seats, which also removes the incumbent's price anchor.

nodes.label: No finalist is not no players
nodes.text: Financial tooling, sales enablement and accounting are thin in finalists and thick in entrants. What is missing from those branches is a winner, not a founder, which is the opposite of an underserved market.
nodes.rationale: Gil states both halves for these verticals, that the market matters and that there are tons of players with no known winner, but does not distinguish them from a branch that is genuinely empty. The distinction is the inference, and it is what stops a MECE reading of a market map from mistaking a crowd for an opening.
nodes.idea: Rank branches by finalists per player, not by finalists: a branch with many entrants and no winner prices entry at the cost of a distribution war, while a branch with neither entrant nor winner is where the same capital buys the category.

edges.rationale: Gil's vertical-by-vertical run and his $5 trillion sizing are about 150 lines apart in the same answer; treating the $5 trillion as the whole that the vertical cut partitions is the reading that makes both statements one partition.
The host's dimension is set before the whole is sized and by a different speaker, so joining them is an inference across the conversation.
The finalists test is applied inside the vertical cut, so it is a second dimension running across the first rather than a rival to it.

Gil answers a question about vertical markets by filing the foundation model market first. Treating it as a branch of the same cut is the reading that makes the overlap visible; treating it as a preamble would hide it.
Coding is named in the same run of verticals, one line before the vertical-by-vertical remark.

edges.source_quote: And you can go through sort of vertical by vertical. There's a bunch of verticals now we know, a bridge for healthcare and maybe commier.

edges.rationale: Legal is filed in the same run-through a dozen lines later, after the hosts prompt for more.
The but then that opens the contested markets continues the same enumeration, so financial tooling is a branch of the same cut.
Named in the same breath as financial tooling and on the same footing.
The branch added to close the partition; it exists only because the cut is supposed to be collectively exhaustive.
Generalised from one company into a branch of the same cut, so that the part of the whole AI does not take is visible rather than assumed away.

edges.source_quote: We know that for the foundation model market. We know it's anthropic, open AI, Google, perhaps XAI, meta, a few others, mistraw, whatever.
We know for coding, it's cognition, cursor, and then the foundation model companies in Microsoft.
There's a bunch of verticals now we know, a bridge for healthcare and maybe commier.

edges.rationale: The legal branch and the legal-never-bought-software remark are about 110 lines apart, and the company is named only as RV; placing it in the branch is a reading of the transcript, not a stated placement.
The branch was generalised from this company, so the containment is the inference read back.
Customer support is named as a market but never given finalists, so it sits in the residual branch: a service line inside the whole with nobody filed against it.
The model branch is a layer, not a vertical, so it cuts across every other branch.
The coding branch contains the model companies by Gil's own list, so the two branches share members.
If AI means consumer, roll-ups and vertical SaaS at once, then AI is not a branch of any cut; the remark is aimed at investing trends, and applying it to this partition is the inference.
What is absent from the residual branch is any named contender at all.
The software-free trades are inside the residual branch and are the part of it with no incumbent to displace.
The labor half is missing from the cut itself rather than from any one branch, which is why no branch is sized correctly.
What financial tooling lacks is a winner, and Gil says so; that this is not the same absence as an empty branch is the inference.
Same absence in accounting and sales enablement, filed by Gil on the same footing.
The settled end of the second cut: a branch where the finalists are known.
The open end of the second cut: a branch where the winners are not known.
The residual exists only because the stated whole is far larger than the named branches.
The stated $5 trillion is the denominator the coverage claim is measured against.
The enumeration Gil offers is what the coverage claim counts; he presents it as illustrative, which is why the confidence is not higher.
The one worked case of a software-free vertical becoming buyable is the whole evidential base for the screen.
Gil's own re-pricing of customer support from seats to work done is the stated instance of the missing dimension.
Tons of players with no known winner is stated for this branch, and it is the fact the distinction rests on.
The model companies appear inside the coding list, which is the double count itself.
The host had put the model layer outside the vertical question, which is what makes its reappearance a mixed cut rather than a choice.
